title: Will Republicans receive above 8% of the Black vote in the 2026 national U.S. House exit poll?
rules: If the Republican share of the Black vote in the 2026 national U.S. House exit poll is above 8%, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary: The value is the percentage shown in the Republican (or Rep.) column of the aggregate Black row in the national U.S. House exit poll table. The primary resolution source is the CNN figure displayed at exactly 12:00 PM ET on November 6, 2026. If unavailable, CNN remains the primary source for 24 hours after that time. If it remains unavailable, use CBS News followed by ABC News through 11:59 PM ET on November 7, 2026.

blind.reasoning: In every midterm exit poll since 2006, Republicans have taken at least about 9% of the Black House vote, including in the 2018 Democratic wave, and recent cycles were higher (about 12-13% in 2022 and 2024). Pre-election 2026 polls show Republicans at 7-8% of Black voters with many undecided; once undecideds are split, as exit polls effectively do, that works out to roughly 9-11%. The main risk is that a historic anti-Trump wave pushes the figure to exactly 8% or lower, since the line is only one point away.
blind.falsifier: CNN's national House exit poll on Nov 6, 2026 shows the Republican share of Black voters at 8% or lower, for example a 90-8 or 91-7 split.

final.reasoning: The market's 0.78 midpoint is very close to my independent estimate of 0.76. Betting NO would mean selling at the 0.76 bid, which equals my probability, so there's no edge on either side and I'm passing.
